clinician.final_diagnosis: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) with pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs) presenting with acute cerebellar ischemic stroke secondary to paradoxical embolism
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old white woman presented with acute seizures and transient left hemiparesis in the context of a chronic clinical syndrome characterized by: (1) repeated episodes of epistaxis with severe iron deficiency anemia, (2) exertional dyspnea, (3) cutaneous telangiectases on the face, (4) pale skin and nail cyanosis, and (5) severe hypoxemia (O2 saturation 82% on ambient air). Brain MRI on admission revealed acute ischemic stroke in the cerebellum with diffusion weighted imaging signal intensity without contrast enhancement. Chest CT imaging identified dilated vessels in the right upper and lower pulmonary lobes consistent with pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs). Abdominal CT was unremarkable. Gastroduodenoscopy and colonoscopy were normal, but capsule endoscopy documented multiple telangiectasias in the jejunum, confirming visceral vascular malformations. The patient received blood transfusion and oral iron supplementation. Right heart catheterization with angiography confirmed the PAVMs and the feeding arteries were successfully embolized via coil occlusion, excluding the PAVMs from the pulmonary circulation. The clinical presentation, imaging findings, and endoscopic evidence of visceral vascular malformations are consistent with HHT, with the acute cerebellar stroke likely resulting from paradoxical embolism through the pulmonary AVMs.
